subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should this mixed Telegram report stay as a coordinated tracker, or should maintainers split it between the existing backed-follow-up/message-tool lifecycle trackers and a focused Linux exec-process repro?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but choosing whether to enforce terse action-only final replies and whether raw shell `pkill` self-matching should be handled by product guidance, process tooling, or a supervisor change is maintainer policy.

options.title: Split And Route
options.body: Use this report as linked evidence, move the follow-up behavior to the existing policy/lifecycle trackers, and ask for a focused Linux exec repro before process-control repair.

options.title: Keep Coordinated Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella for a cross-surface UX fix, accepting that implementation should wait for maintainer-scoped acceptance criteria.

options.title: Close As Duplicates After Linking
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide the pkill symptom is fully covered by the open kill-tree tracker and the Telegram behavior by the existing follow-up trackers.

recommendation.title: Split And Route
recommendation.body: Use this report as linked evidence, move the follow-up behavior to the existing policy/lifecycle trackers, and ask for a focused Linux exec repro before process-control repair.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest recent history across auto-reply delivery and process-runtime cleanup touched by the two halves of the report.
